@@U02946@@
And I’m certain that in the months and years
you've stored up all kinds of experience.

@@U02948@@
Experience!
Smoke in the wind is more like it!
Not equal to the mind of man.
Confess: what’s known as knowledge
isn't worth the knowing.

@@U02950@@
(After a pause.)

@@U02951@@
Yes, I suspected it long ago.
I was a fool; and now I see how
shallow and silly I am.

@@U02953@@
Glad to hear it. You're talking sense.
The first old-timer I’ve known to be reasonable!

@@U02955@@
I’ve searched for buried golden treasures,
and come back with dust and ashes.

@@U02957@@
Admit it,
that bald head of yours
is worth no more than those
skulls over there!

@@U02959@@
(Genially.)

@@U02960@@
I trust, my friend,
you don’t know how rude you are.

@@U02962@@
To be polite in German is to be a liar.
(梅菲斯特 has been inching closer to the proscenium in his
wheelchair.)
translation:
@@U02946@@
我确信在未来的岁月里
你已经积累了各种经验。

@@U02948@@
经验！
风中的烟雾更像了！
不等于人心。
承认：什么叫知识
不值得知道。

@@U02950@@
（停顿后。）

@@U02951@@
是的，我很久以前就怀疑过。
我是个傻瓜；现在我明白了
我是个浅薄又愚蠢的人。

@@U02953@@
很高兴听到这个消息。你说的是有道理的。
我认识的第一个讲道理的老前辈！

@@U02955@@
我寻找埋藏的黄金宝藏，
并带着灰尘和灰烬回来。

@@U02957@@
承认吧，
你的那个光头
不比那些值钱
那里有骷髅！

@@U02959@@
（亲切地。）

@@U02960@@
我相信，我的朋友，
你不知道自己有多粗鲁。

@@U02962@@
在德语中，有礼貌就等于说谎。
（梅菲斯特在他的舞台上慢慢地接近舞台
轮椅。）
